description: Shared Renovate policy for GreenJimmy sites. Extend with { "extends": ["github>GreenJimmy/renovate-config"] }.

packageRules.description: Group all non-major production updates into one pull request.
Group all non-major dev updates into one pull request.

Engine ranges are floors, not pins. The global rangeStrategy bump rewrote node 24.x to 24.21.0, and with engine-strict that fails every install on a host running any other 24.x (Vercel, Railway's node:24-slim). Leave the range alone while the new version satisfies it; .nvmrc and packageManager still move.
Group GitHub Actions, including majors — these are small and easy to read.
Majors are never automerged. The framework stack breaks on majors and each needs reading.

pnpm overrides pin a security floor for a transitive dependency, not a version to track. Raising one to a new major forces an incompatible API on whichever package pinned the old line, breaking a dependency that was never ours to upgrade. In-range updates still flow, so the floor keeps rising as advisories are fixed. Matched on the file rather than a depType because every override lives in pnpm-workspace.yaml and nothing else there needs majors held.

Override floors in pnpm-workspace.yaml are a one-line version bump covered by the full CI run, and they sat open for weeks in every repo waiting for a human (seven open PRs per repo on 2026-10-14). Automerge the non-major ones like the production and development groups; majors stay disabled by the rule above. Matching the file also lets the next+react group automerge, since its branch carries the next@<x override line and a group only automerges when every update in it may.
The packageManager pin (pnpm@x.y.z) is the version CI and the Dockerfile install; non-major bumps are mechanical and CI-covered.
Node minor and patch updates (.nvmrc and the Dockerfile base image) run the full CI matrix on the new runtime before merging; majors stay held.
Keep the framework stack together so its pieces move as a set.
Clerk ships auth changes across several packages at once.
Prisma's client and CLI must move together or generate breaks.

eslint-config-next still pulls eslint-plugin-react 7.37.x, which peers on eslint <=9 and calls the context.getFilename() API that ESLint 10 removed. Raise when eslint-config-next ships an ESLint 10 compatible react plugin.
pg 8.23.0 puts a non-string into the startup packet when driven by @prisma/adapter-pg, so every connection dies in pg-protocol addCString with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE. Raise when the two agree again.
typescript-eslint peers on typescript <6.1.0, so TS 7 breaks pnpm lint. Raise this when typescript-eslint ships TS 7 support (typescript-eslint#10940).

lockFileMaintenance.description: Lock file maintenance is exempt from the release-age gate, like vulnerabilityAlerts above. A refreshed lock almost always resolves something published in the last 24 hours, so renovate/stability-days sat pending on every lock file PR and each rebase reset the clock; the automerge never fired and the weekly review merged them by hand. The lock only moves inside ranges the manifests already allow, so the gate protected nothing here. The window is the same Saturday-evening-to-Sunday-morning one as the top-level schedule, both halves restricted to days 1-7 so it lands on or just before the first Sunday of the month.
